claims_disputed.claim: Graph expansion is the main source of gain; delivering graph evidence inline beats separate graph tools.
claims_disputed.reason: The first half rests on one MuLocBench Acc@5 ablation without variance (Table 3). The second half, inline vs separate tools, is never tested in a controlled way: no arm exposes the same sidecar graph as a separate tool. CoSIL and LocAgent are different systems with their own scaffolds, and the LocAgent reproduction looks broken (App. B Table 4: function-level Acc@1 5.0 and Acc@5 11.7 against file-level Acc@1 56.0), so the cross-system gap cannot be attributed to the interface.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The lexical-only arm loses: 'w/o All modules' scores 46.8 vs 55.7 Acc@5 (Table 3), and Fig. 1 shows recall rising when graph augmentation is switched on. Lexical anchoring is never compared with another anchoring method. Lexical CLI agents do beat the graph-tool agents in Table 1, but across uncontrolled systems. Lexical search is necessary but not sufficient here, which makes the evidence mixed rather than a win for P05.
Keeping the tool catalog unchanged is a design property of LARGER (§4, App. E.4). No experiment varies catalog size or compares the same graph exposed through a new tool.

missed_issues: Internal inconsistency: OpenHands scores differ between Table 1 and App. B for the same metrics. On LocBench, Table 1 gives Acc@1/Acc@5/Rec@5 of 57.7/67.5/75.3, while Table 4 gives 31.1/35.9/40.1. On MuLocBench, Table 1 gives 27.3/43.7/57.6, while Table 5 gives 16.3/26.4/33.7.

App. B.1: 186 of 560 LocBench instances 'failed with API authentication errors and are excluded' from LARGER's telemetry. The paper does not say whether Table 1's LocBench accuracy and the 60.0 s vs 129.2 s runtime comparison use 374 or 560 instances. If 374, the headline +11.8 compares different instance sets.

novelty_inflation: Theorems 1–2 and Proposition 1 are near-tautological. A superset context has at least the recall under an assumed fixed query stream, an assumption the paper itself says is violated in practice (§4.3 remark).

The host CLI agent for LARGER is never named; App. B.1 mentions 'step_finish' telemetry and run names like 'enhanced_nexus_v2'. The same-harness no-graph baseline appears only as one ablation number (MuLocBench Acc@5 46.8), not in Table 1. Codex and Claude Code run 'under their native interfaces' (Table 6), so prompts and runtimes are not matched with LARGER's localization prompt.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with P07 supports, which the on/off toggles and the graph-expansion ablation back. The 'inline beats graph tools' thesis rests on uncontrolled cross-system comparisons with a likely broken LocAgent run. Inconsistent OpenHands tables and partial LocBench coverage further lower rigor.
